title: How early should you arrive at East Midlands Airport?
author: Matt
cover_image_alt: A row of hard-shell suitcases with colourful backpacks on top, lined up against a dark wall
intro: About two hours before a flight is enough at East Midlands most of the time, and a little more if you're dropping a bag in the school holidays. Here's how to work it out, with the drop-off charge and the bus links.
seo_title: East Midlands Airport: arrive 2 hours before? (2026)
seo_description: About 2 hours before most flights, up to 2½ with bags at peak times. East Midlands security, liquids, the drop-off charge and the Skylink bus.

sections.heading: The short answer
sections.text:
- **Hand luggage only:** about 2 hours
- **Bags to drop:** 2 to 2½ hours
- **Peak mornings:** add 30 minutes
- **School holidays:** add 30 to 60 min

That's the timing most guides and airlines suggest for East Midlands, checked in October 2026. Your airline's bag drop and gate deadlines are the ones that count, and they're on your booking. Procedures change, so check the airport's and the airline's current guidance before you go.

sections.heading: A smaller, quicker airport
sections.text:
East Midlands has one terminal and is far smaller than Manchester or Birmingham, which is why many people from Nottingham, Derby and Leicester choose it. The airport says the vast majority of passengers get through security in under 15 minutes.

That's an average, though. Like other holiday airports, it's busiest in the first wave of flights in the early morning, and in the school holidays, when Jet2 and Ryanair sun flights all leave at once. A 6am flight on the first Saturday of the summer holidays is a very different experience from a Tuesday lunchtime in November.

| Trip | Flight | Arrive |
| --- | --- | --- |
| City break, hand luggage only | Midday, midweek | **1½ to 2 hours** before |
| Sun holiday, bags to drop | 6am in July | **2½ hours** before |
| Winter sun, bags to drop | Saturday in February half term | **2 to 2½ hours** before |

sections.heading: Bag drop and boarding
sections.text:
If you're checking a bag, the bag drop deadline is the one to plan around, and airlines don't bend it. Budget airlines usually close bag drop 40 to 60 minutes before departure, and your exact deadline is in your booking.

The gate closes earlier than the departure time too, often about 30 minutes before. At a small airport the walk to the gate is short, but don't leave it to the last call.

Tip: if you're travelling with hand luggage only and checked in online, you can go straight to security. That's the main reason two hours is plenty for most city breaks.

sections.heading: Security and liquids
sections.image_alt: A four-engined passenger jet climbing into a clear blue sky
sections.image_caption: Most East Midlands flights are short-haul, to Europe and the Canaries.
sections.text:
East Midlands has new scanners on its security lanes, so you can usually leave your liquids and laptop in your bag. The size limit hasn't changed, though: according to the airport, liquids must still be in containers of 100ml or less, and the clear plastic bag is no longer needed.

Watch out: you may hear that the 100ml rule has gone at UK airports. That's true at some, but not at East Midlands, and the airport you fly home from may have different rules again. Pack to the 100ml limit and you'll be fine at both ends.

sections.heading: Getting there and dropping off
sections.text:
- **By bus:** the Skylink Express runs between Nottingham and the airport around the clock, via Beeston and Long Eaton. Other Skylink routes serve Derby and Leicester; check current times with the operator.
- **By train:** East Midlands Parkway is the nearest station, with a short road transfer to the airport.
- **Drop-off:** the drop-off area outside the terminal is charged, at around £5 for a short stop, with a penalty if you don't pay online in time. Check the current price and how to pay on the airport's website.
- **Parking:** pre-booking is much cheaper than turning up.

If you're relying on the bus for an early flight, check the timetable for the hour you need, as night services are less frequent.

sections.heading: Five ways to make the airport easier
sections.text:
- **Check in online** and keep your boarding pass on your phone.
- **Travel with hand luggage only** if you can.
- **Work back from your bag drop deadline**, not the departure time.
- **Pay for drop-off straight away**, so you don't forget and get a fine.
- **Allow longer in the school holidays**, especially on early mornings.

sections.heading: Where could you go from East Midlands?
sections.text:
East Midlands is mainly a Ryanair and Jet2 airport, with flights to the Mediterranean, the Canaries and European cities. For winter sun, look at [Tenerife](/destinations/tenerife) or [Lanzarote](/destinations/lanzarote), and for a city break, [Krakow](/destinations/krakow) or [Budapest](/destinations/budapest).

Our guide to [direct flights from East Midlands](/blog/where-can-you-fly-direct-from-east-midlands-airport) has the full list. If you're stuck choosing, read our guide to [deciding where to go on holiday](/how-to-decide-where-to-go-on-holiday), or put everyone's ideas into a draw.

faqs.question: How early should I get to East Midlands Airport?
faqs.answer: About two hours before most flights, and up to two and a half if you have a bag to drop on a busy morning or in the school holidays.

faqs.question: Is 2 hours enough at East Midlands Airport?
faqs.answer: Usually, yes. The airport says most passengers clear security in under 15 minutes, though early mornings in the school holidays are busier.

faqs.question: Is the 100ml liquid rule still in place at East Midlands Airport?
faqs.answer: Yes. According to the airport, liquids must be in containers of 100ml or less, but they can stay in your bag and you no longer need a plastic bag.

faqs.question: How do you get to East Midlands Airport by bus?
faqs.answer: The Skylink Express runs between Nottingham and the airport around the clock. Check the operator's timetable for routes from Derby and Leicester.
